root_cause.text: fsnotify’s connector inode-reference accounting was split across add/remove paths incorrectly, so `fsnotify_recalc_mask()` could clear `FSNOTIFY_CONN_FLAG_HAS_IREF` and return an inode object from `__fsnotify_recalc_mask()` without the caller releasing it, leaking the inode reference in the fsnotify mark connector code.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `__fsnotify_recalc_mask()` to return only a boolean want_iref, adds `fsnotify_recalc_mask_set_iref()` for the add/modify path, and moves the HAS_IREF-clearing/release logic to `fsnotify_recalc_mask_clear_iref()` called from `fsnotify_put_mark()`; the commit message explicitly says `fsnotify_recalc_mask() fails to handle the return value of __fsnotify_recalc_mask()` and that `iput()`/`fsnotify_put_sb_watched_objects()` were never called when HAS_IREF transitioned true->false.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the return type of `__fsnotify_recalc_mask()` to correctly report whether any mark requires an inode reference.
intent_record.what: The function `__fsnotify_recalc_mask()` was changed from returning `void *` to returning `bool`, and a new multi-line comment was added above it describing that it calculates the mask of events for a list of marks and returns whether any attached marks want to hold an inode reference.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now has a boolean return type that can explicitly communicate whether inode reference retention is needed, rather than using an inappropriate pointer return type; this clarifies and enables correct use of the result by callers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refine fsnotify mask recalculation into attach and detach paths to avoid incorrect inode reference handling under concurrent mark updates.
intent_record.what: The code splits the old mask/iref recomputation logic into a common helper and two wrappers: it keeps `__fsnotify_recalc_mask()` returning `want_iref`, adds `fsnotify_recalc_mask_set_iref()` which preserves an existing inode reference by OR-ing `__fsnotify_recalc_mask(conn)` with `conn->flags & FSNOTIFY_CONN_FLAG_HAS_IREF`, and adds `fsnotify_recalc_mask_clear_iref()` which calls `__fsnotify_recalc_mask(conn)` and then `fsnotify_update_iref(conn, want_iref)` for detach paths.
intent_record.how: At runtime, attach/modify operations now avoid dropping an inode reference too aggressively when a concurrent state change makes the mask calculation temporarily say no reference is needed, while detach operations still clear the reference only when the recalculated mask truly no longer requires it. This changes reference-management behavior to better match concurrent mark updates and prevent incorrect iref transitions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update fsnotify mask recalculation to use the inode-reference-aware helper so mask updates maintain the correct connector state.
intent_record.what: Inside fsnotify_recalc_mask(), the call to __fsnotify_recalc_mask(conn) was replaced with fsnotify_recalc_mask_set_iref(conn) while holding conn->lock; the surrounding update_children logic was left unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the recalculation path now uses a variant that also sets the inode reference behavior associated with the mask update, rather than only recomputing the mask. This changes the side effects of mask recalculation and likely ensures the connector/inode state is updated correctly during watch mask changes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the mask recalculation helper that also clears the connector iref when dropping a fsnotify mark.
intent_record.what: In fsnotify_put_mark(), the call that assigned objp was changed from __fsnotify_recalc_mask(conn) to fsnotify_recalc_mask_clear_iref(conn). The surrounding logic and assignments remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, releasing a mark now uses a different mask-recalculation helper that also clears the iref state for the connector. This changes the cleanup path for detached marks so the internal reference-related state is updated as part of recomputing the watch mask.
